chunks: First: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad ibn Uramah al-Qummi from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom, I asked our companions about what I intend to ask you, but I did not find an answer with them, and I have been compelled to ask you. Sa'd ibn Sa'd left a will to me, and in his will he said: 'Perform Hajj on my behalf,' vaguely, without specifying. So what should I do?' He said: 'My answer will come to you in your book,' so he wrote: 'Perform Hajj as long as there is wealth remaining to carry it.'

Second: As for what Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from al-Abbas from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi Khalid who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who willed that Hajj be performed on his behalf vaguely. He said: 'Hajj is performed on his behalf as long as something remains from his third [of the estate]. This does not contradict the first report, because that which he has from his wealth is the third, which is what was specified in the first report, and there is no contradiction between the two reports.'
ai.seo_question: How much of a deceased person's estate should be used for Hajj if the will is vague?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) resolves a legal ambiguity regarding Hajj on behalf of the deceased when the will specifies the act but not the amount. He clarifies that the executor should utilize the remaining balance of the estate's one-third share, which is the standard portion allocated for bequests, thereby harmonizing the vague instruction with established inheritance principles. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential approach to interpreting ambiguous testaments by anchoring them in the fixed shares of the estate.
